extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism layer from SYTOX assay, MD simulation, CD spectroscopy, figure captions, and Results/Discussion prose.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CaD23 directly permeabilized S. aureus membranes in the SYTOX green uptake assay at 50 μg/mL (2x MIC), with about 60% fluorescence increase within seconds and about 80% membrane permeabilization by around 8 min.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CaD23 against Staphylococcus aureus ATCC SA29213
mechanism_claims.limitations: Direct experimental mechanism evidence is for S. aureus ATCC SA29213 membrane permeabilization; it does not prove the same magnitude for all tested bacteria.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: MD simulations support stronger CaD23 interaction with the bacterial membrane model than the mammalian membrane model, including closer peptide-membrane distance and deeper interaction during the last 400 ns analysis window.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CaD23 in model bacterial versus mammalian membranes
mechanism_claims.limitations: Computational model supports membrane interaction and selectivity hypotheses; it is not an independent in vitro killing endpoint.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CD spectroscopy and MD simulations indicate CaD23 is random coil in water and becomes alpha-helical in membrane-mimetic/TFE conditions, with stronger alpha-helical folding near the bacterial membrane model.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Secondary-structure evidence supports, but does not by itself establish, the antimicrobial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper interprets cationicity, alpha-helicity, amphiphilicity, and hydrophobicity, including C-terminal Trp18 interaction with the bacterial membrane, as contributors to antimicrobial action.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an author interpretation from MD and CD context; it is preserved as design rationale rather than a separate direct mechanism assay.
